Rashi on Yevamot 17a:11:1.english: How [does] the wife of his brother who was not in his world - exempt her rival wife?

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:11:2.hebrew: ונולד להם אח - ומצאה זקוקה ליבם, ועליו אסורה משום אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:11:2.english: And a brother was born to them - And he [the newborn brother] found her bound to the levir, and to him she is forbidden on account of [being] the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:11:3.hebrew: ואח"כ ייבם השני את אשת אחיו - ולו אשה אחרת, ומת:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:11:3.english: And afterward, the second [brother] took his brother's wife in levirate marriage - and he had another wife, and he died.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:11:4.english: The first [widow] - This is the wife of Reuven [the first brother], who had already fallen before him [the second brother] once before.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:11:5.english: Goes out - And is exempt from this [brother] because [she is] the wife of his brother who was not in his world, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:12:1.hebrew: עשה בה - זה שמת מאמר, ולא הספיק לכונסה עד שמת:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:12:1.english: He performed with her - [that is,] this [brother] who died [performed] levirate betrothal (ma'amar), and did not manage to consummate the marriage with her before he died.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:12:2.hebrew: שניה חולצת - ולא מיפטרא משום צרת ערוה, דלאו צרתה ממש היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:12:2.english: The second [wife] performs ḥalitza - And she is not exempt on account of [being] the rival wife of a forbidden relative, because she is not actually her rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:12:3.hebrew: ולא מתייבמת - דמאמר קונה מקצת, והויא צרת ערוה במקצת מדרבנן:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:12:3.english: And she may not enter into levirate marriage - Because levirate betrothal [ma'amar] acquires [her] partially, and she is partially the rival wife of a forbidden relative [ervah] by rabbinic decree.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:13:1.hebrew: מאן דתני ראשונה - מאן דקרי לה ראשונה להך שנפלה לפני לוי שני פעמים לא משתבש, ומאן דקרי לה שניה לא משתבש:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:13:1.english: He who taught "first" - He who calls her "first" — [referring to] this [woman] who fell [for levirate marriage] before Levi twice — is not mistaken, and he who calls her "second" is not mistaken.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:1:1.english: This is Ḥadyab, the river of Gozan, etc., Mushkhei, Ḥidkei, and Domakya:

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:1:2.hebrew: לפסול - רובן ממזרים, שנטמעו עשרת השבטים בעובדות כוכבים, ובניהן הרי הן כישראלים ונוהג בהן איסור ממזרות. והן לא נזהרו, ונשאו זה אחותו או בתו, והרי הן ממזרים:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:1:2.english: For disqualification - Most of them are mamzerim, for the Ten Tribes assimilated among the idolatresses, and their children are [considered] like Israelites, and the prohibition of mamzerut applies to them. Yet they were not careful, and one married his sister or his daughter, and thus they are mamzerim.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:2:1.hebrew: כי אמריתה קמיה דשמואל - עד השתא מילתיה דרב יהודה (משמיה דרב אסי קאמר, ואחר פטירתו של רב אסי בא לפני שמואל), וקאמר: כי הדר אמריתה להא דרב אסי קמיה דשמואל, דחוששין לקדושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:2:1.english: When I said it before Shmuel - Until now, [this was] Rav Yehuda's statement (he was saying [it] in the name of Rav Asi, and after Rav Asi's passing he came before Shmuel), and he says: When I subsequently said this [statement] of Rav Asi before Shmuel, that we are concerned for betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:2:2.hebrew: אמר בנך הבא מישראלית קרוי בנך ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה - דנפקא לן מכי יסיר את בנך מאחרי (דברים ז׳:ד׳), ולא כתיב כי תסיר את בנך. אלמא לאו אבתו לא תקח לבנך מהדר, דא"כ היה לו לומר כי העובדת כוכבים תסיר. ש"מ דאי נמי יולדת בן לעבודת כוכבים, לא בנך מיקרי ולא קרינן ביה כי תסיר את בנך. הילכך, עובדי כוכבים גמורים הם:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:2:2.english: He said: Your son from an Israelite woman is called your son, and your son from an idolatrous woman is not called your son, rather her son - For we derive [this] from "For he will turn your son away from following Me" (Deuteronomy 7:4), and it is not written "For she will turn your son away." Evidently, [the verse] is not referring back to "his daughter you shall not take for your son," for if so, it should have said "for the idolatrous woman will turn [him] away." Learn from this that even if she bears a son to idolatry, he is not called "your son," and we do not apply to him "For she will turn your son away." Therefore, they are complete idolaters.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:1.english: And aren't there daughters - who were taken captive, and idolaters married them and fathered [children] from them.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:2.hebrew: ואמר רבינא - לקמן בפ"ב (יבמות דף כג.): בן בתך הבא מן העובד כוכבים קרוי בנך, דכתיב "בתך לא תתן לבנו כי יסיר את בנך מאחרי", מדלא כתב "כי תסיר", ש"מ דאבתך לא תתן לבנו קאי. וה"ק: שמא תלד לו בן, ויסירנו האב מאחרי, וקא קרי ליה "בנך", וליחוש לקידושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:2.english: And Ravina said - Later, in the second chapter (Yevamot 23a), [it is stated that] the son of your daughter from an idolater is called your son, as it is written: "Your daughter you shall not give to his son [...] for he will turn your son away from following Me." Since it did not write "for she will turn away," learn from this that [the verse] refers to "your daughter you shall not give to his son." And this is what [Scripture] is saying: perhaps she will bear him a son, and the father will turn him away from following Me, and [Scripture] calls him "your son" — so let us be concerned about betrothal!

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:3.english: Of that generation - Of the ten tribes.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:4.hebrew: איצטרויי איצטרו - נבקע רחמן מלקלוט זרע, ונעשו עקרות:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:4.english: They became barren - Their wombs split, [preventing them] from absorbing seed, and they became barren.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:5.hebrew: איצטרו - לשון ביקוע, כמו טיליא חריפי דמצרי זיקי (ע"ז ד' ל.), וכמו ציריא דחיטי (פסחים דף מ:):
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:3:5.english: They were split - [This is] an expression of splitting, like [in] "acrid wine that bursts wineskins" (Avodah Zarah 30a) and like "split wheat" (Pesachim 40b).

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:5:1.english: A Festival day - Because they [the inhabitants of Tarmod] are mamzerim, and they assimilate into Israel and disqualify them.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:5:2.hebrew: היינו תרמוד היינו תמוד - ודקאמר הא חרוב, לא חריב כולה:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:5:2.english: Tarmod is [the same as] Tamud - And [as for] what it said, "But it has [already] been destroyed," it was not destroyed in its entirety.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:5:3.hebrew: דאיכפולי איכפול - כשחרבה מכאן, נכפלה וניבנית מכאן:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:5:3.english: That it was doubled - When it was destroyed from here, it was doubled and rebuilt from there.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:6:1.english: And he was [engaged] - [He was] raising difficulties.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:6:2.hebrew: אמר - עולא עליה דרב המנונא, מה גברא ומה גברא — כמה הוא גדול:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:6:2.english: He said - Ulla [said] about Rav Hamnuna: "What a man and what a man" — how great he is.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:6:3.english: Were it not that Harpanya is his town - For they are not of [pure] lineage.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:7:1.english: That all turn there - All disqualified [persons] who do not find a wife turn and go there.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:7:2.hebrew: והיא עמוקה - ורעה לדבר זה יותר מגיהנם, דאילו ליורדי גיהנם איכא תקנתא, דכתיב: "מיד שאול אפדם ממות אגאלם", ואילו פסולי דידהו לית להו תקנתא:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:7:2.english: And it is deeper - and worse in this matter than Gehinnom, for those who descend to Gehinnom have a remedy, as it is written: "From the hand of the netherworld I will ransom them, from death I will redeem them" [Hosea 13:14], whereas their disqualified ones have no remedy.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:8:1.hebrew: משום פסולי דמישון - שקרובה לה ומתערבין בהן, ואמר בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קידושין עא:): מישון מתה, והתם מפרש פסולייהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:8:1.english: Due to those disqualified from Meishon - Because [Meishon] is close to [Harpanya] and they intermarry with them; and [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 71b): "Meishon is dead," and there it explains their disqualification.

Rashi on Yevamot 17a:9:1.hebrew: קבא רבא וקבא זוטא - איפה גדולה ואיפה קטנה, שניהם מעוותים; כלומר, כל הפסולין מתגלגלים ויורדים לשאול, ומשאול לתרמוד, כלומר ששאול גבוה מתרמוד, ומתגלגל משאול לתרמוד. וטעמא כדלעיל, דאילו ליורדי גיהנם איכא תקנתא, ולפסול דידהו אין טהרה:
Rashi on Yevamot 17a:9:1.english: A large kav and a small kav - A large ephah and a small ephah, both of them distorted [measures]; that is to say, all the disqualified ones roll and descend to Sheol, and from Sheol to Tarmod — meaning that Sheol is higher than Tarmod, and [one] rolls from Sheol to Tarmod. And the reason is as [stated] above: for whereas for those who descend to Gehenna there is a remedy, for their disqualification there is no purification.

Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:11:1.hebrew: כיצד - "עשה בה מאמר" — דסיפא (דף יח:) לא אצטריך, דמרישא שמעי' לה; אלא איידי דמתני ליה ברישא, תנא להו נמי בסיפא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:11:1.english: What [is the case] - "He performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal] on her" — [the case] of the latter clause (18b) is not needed, for we infer it from the first clause; rather, since it teaches it in the first clause, it also teaches them in the latter clause.

Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:13:1.hebrew: מאן דתני ראשונה לא משתבש - הכא לא בעי: "מאן דתני ראשונה, אמאי לא תני שניה?", כדדייק בריש מס' ע"ז (דף ב. ושם): "מאן דתני אידיהן, מ"ט לא תני עידיהן?". דהתם בעי משום דה"ל למיתני לשון עדות, כדכתיב: "יתנו עדיהן ויצדקו", ובתר דמשני דתברא עדיף, הדר פריך: "מאן דתני עידיהן, מאי טעמא לא תני אידיהן?":
Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:13:1.english: He who taught "the first" is not mistaken - Here [the Gemara] does not ask: "He who taught 'the first,' why did he not teach 'the second'?" as it infers at the beginning of Tractate Avodah Zarah (2a and there): "He who taught ideihen [with an alef], why did he not teach eideihen [with an ayin]?" For there it asks [this] because it should have taught an expression of testimony, as it is written: "Let them bring their witnesses [edeihem] and be justified" [Isaiah 43:9]; and after it answers that [an expression of] calamity [tevira] is preferable, it goes back and objects: "He who taught eideihen [with an ayin], why did he not teach ideihen [with an alef]?"

Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:2:1.hebrew: ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה - פירש בקונטרס, דמדכתב "כי יסיר" ולא כתב "כי תסיר", משמע דלא קאי א"בתו לא תקח לבנך", דאי יולדת בן לעבודת כוכבים לאו בנך מיקרי, ולא קרינן ביה "כי תסיר את בנך", אלא א"בתך לא תתן לבנו" קאי, וה"ק: שמא תלד בן ויסירנו האב מאחרי, שאותו קרוי "בנך". וקשה לר"ת לפירושו: דפי' "בנך קרוי בנך" היינו בנך הבא מן הישראלית שאביו עובד כוכבים, דעליה קאי "כי יסיר"; וא"כ, אמאי מייתי "ואמר רבינא: בן בתך כו'"? הרי הן ממש דברי שמואל! ורבינא נמי מאי קאמר "ש"מ מדר' יוחנן"? מה שייך לומר "ש"מ", דהן ממש דברי רבי יוחנן! ואומר ר"ת ד"כי יסיר" א"בתו לא תקח לבנך" קאי, והכי קאמר: כי יסיר החותן את בנך מאחרי, והיינו הסרה — שאין הזרע מתייחס אחר בנך אלא אחר העובדת כוכבים, דאין קרוי בנך אלא בנה. ושמואל ורבי יוחנן לא פירשו כלום בעובד כוכבים הבא על בת ישראל, אלא רבינא מדקדק דבן בתך הבא מן העובד כוכבים קרוי בנך: מדלא כתב "כי יסיר את בתך", ש"מ דלית בה הסרה, משום דמתייחס אחריה. ואין נראה לר"י, ד"כי יסיר" משמע כמו הסרה מאת הקב"ה, כדמתרגמי': "ארי יטעי יתה", ודרשי' נמי מ"כי יסיר" לרבות כל המסירים. ועוד פירש ר"ת בע"א: דשמואל ורבי יוחנן דייקי מ"כי יסיר את בנך" — דמשמע דוקא על הסרתו הקפיד הכתוב שלא יטעהו, ולא על הסרת בן בנו, דכיון דבא מן העובדת כוכבים אין קרוי בנך אלא בנה, מדלא כתיב "כי יסירם" או "כי יסיר בנך וזרעו מאחרי"; ורבינא דייק ש"מ בן בתך הבא מן העובד כוכבים קרוי בנך — דדוקא בבנך "כי יסיר את בנך" למעוטי זרעו, אבל בבתך אפי' בזרעו יש לחוש להסרה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:2:1.english: And your son from a gentile woman is not called your son, rather her son - Rashi explained that since [Scripture] wrote "for he will turn away [yasir]" and did not write "for she will turn away [tasir]," this implies that it does not refer to "his daughter you shall not take for your son" — for if she bears a son to idolatry, he is not called "your son," and we do not apply to him "for she will turn away your son" — rather, it refers to "your daughter you shall not give to his son," and this is what [Scripture] is saying: lest she bear a son and the [gentile] father turn him away from following Me, for that [son] is called "your son." And Rabbeinu Tam finds [a difficulty] with his explanation: since [Rashi] explained [that] "your son is called your son" refers to your son who comes from a Jewish woman whose father is a gentile, to whom "for he will turn away" refers — if so, why does [the Gemara] cite "and Ravina said: your daughter's son, etc."? Those are literally Shmuel's very words! And what does Ravina mean as well [by saying], "Learn from this from R. Yochanan"? What relevance is there to say "learn from this," when those are literally R. Yochanan's very words! And Rabbeinu Tam says that "for he will turn away" refers to "his daughter you shall not take for your son," and this is what [Scripture] is saying: "for the father-in-law will turn your son away from following Me" — and that is the turning away, that the offspring is not attributed to your son, but rather to the gentile woman, for [the child] is not called your son, rather her son. And Shmuel and R. Yochanan did not explain anything regarding a gentile who cohabits with a Jewish woman; rather, Ravina deduces that your daughter's son who comes from a gentile is called your son: since [Scripture] did not write "for he will turn away your daughter," learn from this that there is no turning away in her case, because [her offspring] is attributed to her. And this does not appear [correct] to R. Yitzchak, for "for he will turn away" implies turning away from the Holy One, blessed be He, as we translate [in the Targum]: "for he will lead him astray" [arei yat'ei yateih], and we also expound from "for he will turn away" to include all who lead astray. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam explained in another way: that Shmuel and R. Yochanan infer from "for he will turn away your son" — which implies that Scripture was concerned specifically about turning him away, that he should not lead him astray, and not about turning away his son's son, for since he comes from the gentile woman, he is not called your son, rather her son — since it is not written "for he will turn them away" or "for he will turn away your son and his seed from following Me"; and Ravina infers, learn from this [that] your daughter's son who comes from a gentile is called your son — for specifically with respect to your son [does it say] "for he will turn away your son," to exclude his seed, whereas with respect to your daughter, even for her seed there is concern about turning away.

Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:8:1.hebrew: פסולי דמישן משום פסולי דתרמוד - והא דאמר בפרק שני דקדושין (דף מט:): "עשרה קבין עזות ירדו לעולם, תשעה נטלה מישן ואחת כל העולם", פי': לפי שהן ממזרים — הא דלא נקט תרמוד שפסולין יותר: שמא אשתרבוב למישן עד שגדלו יותר מתרמוד, ושמא בתרמוד היו רוב עובדי כוכבים, ובמישן רוב ישראל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:8:1.english: "Those disqualified from Meishon [are unfit] due to those disqualified from Tarmod" - And [regarding] that which [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Kiddushin (49b): "Ten kavs of impudence descended to the world; Meishon took nine and the entire world [took] one" — meaning, because they are mamzerim — [the reason] it did not mention Tarmod, which is more disqualified, [is that] perhaps they spread into Meishon until they grew [more numerous] than [in] Tarmod; or perhaps in Tarmod the majority were idolaters, whereas in Meishon the majority were Jews.

Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:9:1.hebrew: משאול לתרמוד - שאול קורא בבל, לפי שתחילה גלו כולם לבבל — כשרים ופסולים, ומבבל הלכו כל הפסולים לתרמוד, כדאמר בעשרה יוחסין (קדושין סט:) דלא עלה עזרא מבבל עד שעשאה כסולת נקיה. ומונה כסדר שהלכו הפסולים מזו לזו, כמו שהקב הולך ומתגלגל מכאן לכאן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 17a:9:1.english: From Sheol to Tarmod - [The Gemara] calls Babylonia "Sheol," because initially all of them were exiled to Babylonia — [both] those of valid [lineage] and those of disqualified [lineage] — and from Babylonia all the disqualified ones went to Tarmod, as it says in [the chapter] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 69b), that Ezra did not ascend from Babylonia until he made it like sifted fine flour. And [the saying] enumerates [the places] in the order that the disqualified ones went from one to another, just as the kav [measure] goes and rolls from here to there.
